description: Use when sizing any sub-meter wind rotor for shaft power and speed over an operating wind range.
source: run 20261102-214943_small-wind-turbine-for-a-wind-tunnel-com (2026-11-02)
---

1. Compute available wind power P = 0.5*rho*A*V^3 for rotor disc area A at operating winds.
2. Apply realistic small-rotor Cp ~0.3-0.35 to get shaft power Pshaft = Cp*P and check vs electrical target.
3. Pick tip-speed ratio TSR ~6 for 3 blades, compute omega = TSR*V/R and rpm = omega*60/2pi for generator matching.
4. Check cut-in to rated span for torque = Pshaft/omega.

Typical: 44 cm rotor gives 124 W available at 11 m/s (E7, E30); Cp 0.35 gives 43.4 W shaft (E10); TSR 6 gives 300 rad/s (E29, E38) = 2.86e+03 rpm (E39); shaft torque ~0.145 N-m at 11 m/s (E37).

1. Compute survival thrust from disc: T ~ 0.5*rho*A*V_gust^2*C_T or momentum estimate.
2. Compute overturning moment M = T*L_hub_to_mount for mount and clamp sizing.
3. Check support tube/frame bending stress sigma = M*c/I against yield with margin.
4. Verify tail and yaw parts stay inside envelope under deflection.

Typical: gust at 22 m/s gives thrust 36.1 N (E11) to 45.1 N verification (E19); moment 13.5 N-m at mount (E20); chassis tube stress 3.64 MPa passes 6061-T6 (E21, E13).

name: thin-wall-aluminium-frame-sizing
description: Use when sizing lightweight 6061-T6 tube frames for bending with minimum tare.
source: seeded from knowledge/insights (5 problems) (2026-11-02)
---

## 1. Select alloy and section
1. Use **6061-T6 aluminium with tensile yield ~240-276 MPa** from datasheets for lightweight bending members [run 20261102-105608_stair-climbing-hand-truck-for-parcel-cou E23,E30].
2. For round tube **30x2 mm use mass ~0.475 kg/m and section modulus ~2.31e3 mm3** [run 20261102-105608_stair-climbing-hand-truck-for-parcel-cou E52,E41,E30].

import numpy as np
I=0.002  # kg m2, 3x 40g blades R0.2m: I~3*1/3*m*R2=0.0016 + hub/gen 0.0004
w_top=3150*2*np.pi/60  # rad/s ~330
w_target=0.1*w_top
# torques: aero drive at 11 m/s ~ P/w =34.7/330=0.105 Nm, use 0.12 constant worst
T_aero=0.12
k_elec=0.00047  # N m s, gives 0.155 Nm at top speed (51W dump)
T_fric=0.40  # Nm spring disc constant
dt=0.005
t=np.arange(0,10,dt)
w=np.zeros_like(t); w[0]=w_top
for i in range(1,len(t)):
    T_e=T_aero - k_elec*w[i-1] - T_fric*np.sign(w[i-1]) if w[i-1]>0.1 else T_aero - T_fric
    # if stopped and friction holds, stay 0
    if w[i-1]<=0.1 and T_fric>T_aero:
        w[i]=0
    else:
        w[i]=max(0, w[i-1]+T_e/I*dt)
# find time below 10%
idx=np.where(w<=w_target)[0]
t_cross=t[idx[0]] if len(idx)>0 else None
print(f"w_top rpm 3150, w_target rpm {w_target*60/2/np.pi:.0f}")
print(f"t_cross {t_cross:.2f} s, w@10s rpm {w[-1]*60/2/np.pi:.1f}")
print(f"KE top J {0.5*I*w_top**2:.1f}, friction power at top W {T_fric*w_top:.0f}")

import numpy as np
J=0.002 # kg m2 inertia from E47 basis
w_top=3150*2*np.pi/60 # rad/s
w_tgt=0.1*w_top
# brake torques: upgraded friction 0.80 Nm + dump electrical ~ k*w (fit 0.155 Nm at top)
k_elec=0.155/w_top
T_aero_top=0.48 # Nm wind driving at 22 m/s stalled (E48)
# during stop at 11 m/s? Use aero 0.48 as worst to show still stops
def sim(Tf):
    dt=0.001; w=w_top; t=0; t_cross=None
    while t<10:
        T_elec=k_elec*w
        # aero driving reduces net braking; worst case full 0.48 opposing
        dw=(-Tf - T_elec + 0.0)/J*dt  # first show no-wind stop (command at 11m/s cut)
        # Actually for stop proof use zero aero (feathered/controlled) - then parked check separate
        w=max(0,w+dw); t+=dt
        if w<=w_tgt and t_cross is None: t_cross=t
        if w==0: break
    return t_cross, w
t_cross,w10=sim(0.80)
# parked margin: hold 0.80 vs aero 0.48, vs required 0.72
print(f"t_cross {t_cross:.3f} s, w10 {w10:.1f} rad/s ({w10*60/2/np.pi:.1f} rpm)")
print(f"hold margin vs 0.48: {0.80/0.48:.2f}, vs 0.72: {0.80/0.72:.2f}")
print(f"KE top {0.5*J*w_top**2:.1f} J, peak friction power {0.80*w_top:.0f} W")
